title: Model conditional RAM-slot OBJ markers
platforms: EUR original source; Windows executable under Wine
changes: Model two exact one-object OBJ lists selected by the low byte of an original writer and passed through a RAM slot to the original draw; leave E128 publication unchanged.
validation: Source pins and 51015 authenticated E128 manifest spans establish the bounded writer-to-consumer path and no declared source overlap; 345 retained saved boundaries provide no in-range live context. Two focused Windows GNU tests pass under Wine, including six original writer calls with pointer, coordinate, full EWRAM, out-of-stack IWRAM and callee-register guards. Protected ROM and sources pass.

An initial Wine-build receipt returned a stale executable and is rejected for source identity; the corrected guarded build and writer oracle pass. Evidence: target/validation/units/e128-obj-02f414-source-roots-f4o7fxwq/, e128-obj-02f414-retained-roots-v3y2mdwt/, e128-obj-markers-writer-oracle-build-dilgys1i/ and e128-obj-markers-writer-oracle-wine-2enqulxu/.
limitations: Standalone source model only: no published owner, runtime consumption, original draw execution or ordinary scene and full pair. Other OBJ roots, writers, Linux, USA and native Windows remain open; no performance measurements.
